trigger: CH-6 storm-wedge branch leaks a real WindowsFileMechanism with no st-anchor independent of a bounded-lifetime test thread
summary: Unlike CH-8's equivalent branch (whose stopper thread stays blocked inside stop() for exactly as long as a genuine wedge persists), CH-6's joiner thread runs a bounded loop and returns - dropping its st copy - even if the leaked mechanism's internal worker is still genuinely wedged forever afterward. A late callback into &st->log after Ch6/EstLog is destroyed is a compound-conditioned (storm-wedge fires AND joiner completes AND worker later dispatches), test-process-local heap UAF - would likely be caught by ASan, not production-reachable.
classification_rationale: An ownership/lifetime claim about the actual test code, independently confirmed by unhappy-path (4659-up-3).

adjudication_rationale: Fixed in bbde0ffff's parent commit 4550ad96a: captured st in mech->start()'s fire/fault lambdas so the mechanism object itself anchors st for as long as it exists. cpp-safety re-verified against the actual WindowsFileMechanism::start()/stop() implementation (emit_/fault_ member storage, cleared only after worker_.join() succeeds in stop()) and confirmed the fix is load-bearing, not a no-op - and found a bonus: the same fix transitively closes a second, previously-unnoticed raw-pointer exposure via the established_ sink (also held a dangling-prone raw reference into st->log). quality-engineer independently confirmed the fix is minimal, correctly scoped, and introduces no test-exercise-masking risk.
